title: Finance & Accounts Adventure 3: Break-even & Investment Appraisal
welcome_lead: Today you'll compute break-even, payback, ARR and NPV — four ways to judge an investment.
meta_desc: Business Management Finance: break-even, payback period, average rate of return, net present value.
final_note: You used break-even and three investment appraisal methods to evaluate projects.

concepts.def: Price minus variable cost per unit
Time to recoup the initial outlay
Sum of discounted future cash flows
Rate used to bring future cash to today

walkthroughs.body_html:
Break-even Output = Fixed Costs / Contribution per unit.

Contribution = Price − Variable Cost.

Example: FC $40,000, price $20, VC $10. Contribution = $10. Break-even = 4,000 units.

Margin of safety = Actual sales − Break-even sales. The larger the margin, the safer the firm.

Payback = years to recover outlay. Simple, but ignores cash after payback and time value of money.

Average Rate of Return = (avg annual profit / initial outlay) × 100.

ARR uses profit not cash, and unlike payback, considers project life — but still ignores discounting.

NPV discounts future cash flows by the cost of capital, then subtracts the outlay.

NPV > 0 → accept; NPV < 0 → reject. NPV respects the time value of money but depends heavily on the chosen discount rate.

options: Price − fixed cost

mcqs.q: When might an autocratic leadership style be appropriate?
options: Cash flow only matters at year-end.
Autocratic leaders are dictators who break the law.
In crises requiring quick decisions, when workers are inexperienced, or in highly hierarchical contexts — though it can damage morale long-term.
Autocratic leadership is always wrong and democratic leadership is always right.

mcqs.q: How does HRM differ from traditional personnel management?
options: HRM treats people as a strategic asset and integrates human resource policies with business strategy; personnel management is more administrative and reactive, handling hiring, pay and disputes.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.
HRM and personnel are exactly the same thing — just a name change.
HRM only applies to large multinational companies.

mcqs.q: Why are cash flow and profit different on different time-scales?
options: Cash flow only matters at year-end.
Cash flow and profit are the same thing measured differently.

Profit is recognised when a sale is made (even on credit); cash flow is when money actually moves. A profitable sale today may produce no cash for 60 days while bills are due — creating a cash-flow problem despite profit.
HRM only applies to large multinational companies.
